_comment: POS product name -> Purchase-module par SKU name.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS: the till (Back Office sale products) and the Purchase
module (stock/par SKUs) are named by different people at different times and
they drift. The par model attributes POS volume to par SKUs BY NAME, so every
drifted name silently dropped 100% of that product's demand and the par
collapsed to whatever the safety net held it at.
The proven case: par SKU 'Petits Detours Rose Mediterranee - Bottle' (live par
22.9) only ever matched the POS line 'Petits Detours Rose Mediterranee'
(~3.9/wk, the by-the-bottle line). The by-the-glass line is called 'Petits
Detours Rose' (34.2/wk) and reached nothing, so 90% of the volume vanished and
the model recommended 3.0 for a wine that needs ~22.
Measured scale before this file existed: $54,794 of Stowaway drink sales over
13 weeks reached no par SKU at all.
FORMAT: "<POS product name>": "<par SKU name>", or, when the POS line is a
pour whose size the reporting group cannot imply,
"<POS product name>": {"sku": "<par SKU name>", "serve_ml": 150}.
CROSS-VENUE TARGETS: a target may be prefixed with a venue code —
"stow:Kirin [Keg]" inside the "hg" map (or "hg:..." inside "stow", if it is
ever needed). It means: this till line is poured at THIS venue out of stock
that is held and ordered at THAT venue, against THAT venue's par SKU. The
volume is added to the target venue's par SKU (same unit conversions), and
contributes to NOTHING at the venue that sold it — a POS line feeds exactly
one par SKU in exactly one venue. It is not unattributed: it appears in the
selling venue's unattributed report under `attributed_to_other_venue`, and
the target is validated against the TARGET venue's par universe, so a typo
still fails the build. Only "stow" and "hg" are legal prefixes; a SKU name
that merely contains a colon is left alone.
WHY IT EXISTS: Stowaway and Harry Gatos share some lines. The tap beers
Philter XPA / Grifter Pale / Kirin / Crankshaft IPA / Status Quo / Guinness,
and the Coke and Sprite cans, are ordered centrally on Stowaway's pars but
also pour through the HG till. Those HG sales reached no par SKU anywhere, so
Stowaway's pars under-counted real consumption. Zak, 2026-08-10: "link the hg
tap beers to the stowaway pars, and the coke sprite cans to stowaway pars
too. ignore the juice as we will just order that visually, too hard to track
the stock on those."
THE [HG] SUFFIX RULE — WHY THIS FILE IS SHORTER THAN IT LOOKS. Zak,
2026-08-10: "same as the wines. pretty much any SKU labelled with [HG] is
a harrys SKU that draws from stowaway stock". That is a RULE, not a list,
so it is mechanised in modules/par/model.py (HGSuffixRule) rather than
transcribed here: ANY Harry Gatos till line carrying the '[HG]' suffix has
the suffix stripped and the remainder matched against STOWAWAY's par
universe, tolerating the '- Bottle' / '[Bottle]' / '[Keg]' / 'Can' / 'Tin'
drift between the two catalogues, and its consumption is routed to that
Stowaway par SKU. A NEW [HG] product therefore attributes correctly the
first week it sells and NOBODY HAS TO EDIT THIS FILE.
* AN EXPLICIT ENTRY BELOW ALWAYS BEATS THE RULE. That is the escape
hatch for the one product where 'pretty much any' does not hold — you
correct that product, you do not switch the rule off.
* The rule NEVER GUESSES. If the stripped name matches no Stowaway par
SKU, or matches several with no live par to break the tie, the line is
left unattributed for the coverage guard and listed in the build output
and data/par_unattributed_harry_gatos.json as `hg_suffix_unresolved`,
with the stripped name, so writing the explicit alias is mechanical.
* A line in _intentionally_unattributed is never offered to the rule.
* See data/_par_review/hg_suffix_review.md for the open question this
raises: several [HG] SKUs still hold their own HARRY GATOS par, which
would double-count stock that is really Stowaway's. Nothing has been
changed there — it is a question for Zak.
RULES FOR ADDING AN ENTRY:
* Only map where you are CONFIDENT it is the same physical stock item.
* Glass/nip pour lines map to the '- Bottle' / '[Bottle]' / '[20L]' par SKU;
the model's existing unit conversion then applies. Do NOT pre-convert.
* Tap beer lines map to the '[Keg]' par SKU. schooner/pint -> keg conversion
is applied by the model (modules/par/model.py TAP_SERVE_ML).
* Made-to-order / post-mix drinks that consume no discrete stock unit go in
_intentionally_unattributed, NOT here.
* Cocktails belong to the RECIPE system (data/recipes/*.yaml), NOT here.
Enforced by the unattributed-volume coverage guard in
scripts/build_par_model.py, which fails the build if more than $2,000 of
13-week stock-bearing drink revenue reaches no par SKU.

Alehouse is the contract brewer; 'Fresh is Best' is the customer-facing name. The keg par SKU carried a live par of 4.6 with zero attributed volume, which is the drift signature.
stow.Fresh is Best Summer Lager: Same, via recipe 'Fresh is Best Summer Lager - Schooner/- Pint' -> 'Alehouse Summer Mid [Keg]' (live par 1.2, zero attributed volume).
stow.Guinness Draught: Only Guinness keg in the catalogue. resolve_bulk missed it purely on the trailing word 'Draught'.
stow.Philter Red: 'Philter Red [Keg]' exists in the catalogue but has no live par and no recipe; the POS line is 13.9/wk.
stow.Grifter - \"Omen\" Nitro Stout: Tap line -> 'Omen Stout Nitro [Keg]'. Deliberately NOT 'Grifter Omen Stout Tin' (live par 9.6): the POS line's reporting group is Tap Beer and the name says Nitro, so it is the keg, not the can.
stow.White Light Pure Vodka [House]: House-pour vodka on the 20L cask. The par SKU drops the word 'Pure'.
stow.Petits Detours Rosé: The by-the-glass line for the same wine. The bottle line 'Petits Detours Rosé Mediterranee' already matched; this one did not, and it is 90% of the volume.
stow.Baileys Irish Cream: Par SKU has an apostrophe and a '1L' size token.
stow.Vinada Sparkling Rose: TYPO IN THE PAR SKU NAME: 'Vinada Sparking Rosé [Bottle]' (missing the 'l' in Sparkling). Non-alc sparkling poured by the glass from a 750ml bottle - unit price $10.39 is a glass, and 4.1 glasses/wk against a live par of 0.6 bottles confirms it.
stow.Limoncello: The Liqueurs POS line (nip pour, $9.74) -> the only limoncello bottle in the par book. NOT 'Limoncello Spritz' (a cocktail, already resolved by the recipe book) and NOT the 'Limoncello Bottle - 250ml/700ml' delivery SKUs.

stow.Kahlúa Coffee Liqueur: Par SKU is 'Kahlua [1L]' - no accent, no words 'Coffee Liqueur'. NOT 'Mr Black Coffee Liqueur [Bottle]', which is a different product the fuzzy matcher likes.
stow.Flor De Ca|a 4 Extra Seco: MOJIBAKE IN THE SOURCE: products_weekly.csv carries 'Ca|a' where the POS has 'Caña'. Mapped literally so the volume lands; fix the export encoding and this entry can go.
stow.Tequila Ocho - Single Estate A|ejo: Same mojibake ('A|ejo' = 'Añejo'), plus the par SKU spells it 'Anejo' without the tilde.
stow.4 Pines Kolsch Bottle: The only 4 Pines par SKU is the delivery twin '4 Pines Kolsch Bottle D'. Same physical bottle; the 'D' is a channel marker, not a different stock item.
stow.Bundaberg Ginger Beer: Par SKU carries the size token '[750ml]'.

hg._no_alias_Diet Coke Can: NOT mapped, deliberately. HG sells 'Diet Coke Can' 0.31/wk. Stowaway stocks 'Coke Zero Can', not Diet Coke — there is no Diet Coke SKU anywhere in data/bo_exports/stowaway_products.csv (only Coke, Coke Zero, Sprite in can and 1.25L). Coke Zero and Diet Coke are different products with different formulations and different order codes, so mapping one to the other would put a real Diet Coke order on a Coke Zero par and silently mis-state both. Left in _unmapped_investigate until Zak confirms whether HG's Diet Coke button is actually poured from Coke Zero stock (in which case alias it to 'stow:Coke Zero Can') or whether Diet Coke is a genuine separate line that needs its own stock item.

mari._why_this_map_exists: Zak, 2026-08-10: 'and yes you need to figure out marilynas consumption as well! that all gets lumped into the stowaway lightspeed pars'. Marilyna's has NO till and NO Purchase module — its sales are an attributed slice of the Stowaway till and its stock is Stowaway's stock. It therefore owns no par SKU, and EVERY entry in this map must carry the 'stow:' prefix. A bare target is not 'a Marilyna's par SKU', it is an error, and the build fails on it: par_universe('mari') is the empty set by construction, so unknown_targets() reports any unprefixed value.
mari._why_it_is_empty_today: It is empty because it does not need to be full. MariNameRule resolves a mari till line whose NORMALISED NAME IS a Stowaway par SKU, so the eleven lines that carry real Stowaway stock today — Coke Zero Can 6.85/wk, Coke 1.25L 5.38, Sprite Can 4.85, Coke Can 4.69, Coke Zero 1.25L 3.46, Solo 1.25L 1.54, Sprite 1.25L 1.00, Grifter Pale Ale Cans D 0.92, Grifter Serpents Kiss Can 0.38, Sunkist 1.25L 0.31, 4 Pines Kolsch Bottle D 0.08 — resolve with no file edit, and so will the next one. An entry here is only needed where the rule REFUSES, and every refusal is listed with the near-miss SKU in data/par_unattributed_marilynas.json `auto_unresolved`.
mari._the_work_queue: Thirty-nine mari lines still reach no par SKU and are not pizza: 37 'Delivery Alcohol' lines ($1,843/13wk) and 2 soft drinks ($200/13wk). Most are one exact-name edit away — 'Kuku Sauvignon Blanc D' -> 'stow:Kuku Sauvignon Blanc - Bottle', 'Bundaberg Ginger Beer D' -> 'stow:Bundaberg Ginger Beer [750ml]', 'VB Can D' -> 'stow:VB Tinnie'. They are NOT written here yet on purpose: the loose container-base matcher that would place them automatically is switched OFF for Marilyna's (see MariNameRule), because run over a catalogue that is 80% pizza it also matches the add-on 'Sour Cream' to the 2-litre tub 'Sour Cream [2L]' and 'Status Quo Can D' to a 50-litre keg. Each alias below should be a human confirming the stock is the same, once — not a machine guessing it weekly. Nothing is silent in the meantime: all 39 are in the report with the SKU each would point at.
mari._pizza_is_not_an_alias_problem: 215 mari lines (659 units/wk, $136,281 ex-GST over 13 weeks) are pizzas, pizza add-ons and cocktail jars. They consume Stowaway stock through INGREDIENTS — flour, mozzarella, pepperoni, bases, boxes — so no alias can ever place them and none should be written here. They are classified `needs_recipe`, quantified in data/_par_review/marilynas_recipe_gap.md, and deliberately excluded from the $2,000 unattributed gate.
mari._why_this_block_exists: Marilyna's has no till and no Purchase module: every physical thing it sells comes off STOWAWAY's shelf and is reordered against a Stowaway par SKU. The mari_name_rule already resolves lines whose name matches a stow par SKU exactly; these are the ones where the delivery menu names the same product differently. Until now 39 lines reached no par at all.
mari._evidence_singles: Two independent checks per line, not a name guess. (1) The target is a LIVE stow par SKU - all 27 verified present in _scrape_stow_20260815.json. (2) The implied unit price says it is a single: these run $4.36-$7.27 for the cans and tonics and $19.64-$38.48 for the wine bottles, against Stowaway's own shelf prices for the same products.
mari._evidence_packs: The pack count is STATED IN THE TILL LINE'S OWN NAME ('6-pack', '4-pack'), so it is data, not inference - the same standard the invoice reader applies to a CTN-n note. Price corroborates: Corona single $5.45 vs 6-pack $19.20 = $3.20 a can, Asahi single $6.50 vs 6-pack $21.09 = $3.52 a can. A pack discount, which is what a 6-pack should look like. Booked via `units`, so one ring takes the whole pack off the shelf.
mari._deliberately_left_out: Status Quo Can D - the only 'Status Quo' par SKU is a KEG. A can is not a keg and there is no can par to point at. Pink Galah Can D / Pink Galah 4-pack D, Two Bays GF Pale Can D - no stow par SKU exists for these at all; they need a par created before an alias means anything. Aliasing any of the four would have invented a number.
mari._status_quo_can: RESOLVED 2026-08-15 - see _intentionally_unattributed: the can is real delivery stock, sub-threshold, ad hoc. Question closed by Zak.
